.troupe/prompt.txt:

examples.input: `config set agents.coder '{model: opus}'` (the value the included coder.yaml already gives)

results.1: The two arms differed. One arm: exit 0, silent, nothing changed. The other arm: exit 3, `troupe: write refused: agents.coder: value comes from include /theatre/.troupe/agents/coder.yaml; refusing to replace it`
results.2: The two arms differed. One arm: exit 3, `/theatre/.troupe/agents/coder.yaml: agents.coder: the whole value comes from the include file:agents/coder.yaml; change the included file instead`. The other arm: exit 0, silent, nothing changed
results.3: exit 3, `troupe: error: agents.coder: its whole value comes from include 'file:agents/coder.yaml' in /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml; change the included file instead`
results.4: exit 3, `troupe: agents.coder: value comes from include /theatre/.troupe/agents/coder.yaml; refusing to replace it (change a path inside it instead); no file changed`

examples.input: `config set agents.reviewer '{model: haiku, temperature: 0.3}'` (the same value it already resolves to, through `$ref` plus an override)

results.1: The two arms differed. One arm: exit 0, silent, nothing changed. The other arm: exit 3, `troupe: write refused: agents.reviewer: value comes from include /theatre/.troupe/agents/reviewer.yaml; refusing to replace it`
results.2: The two arms differed. One arm: exit 3, `/theatre/.troupe/agents/reviewer.yaml: agents.reviewer: the whole value comes from the include file:agents/reviewer.yaml; change the included file instead`. The other arm: exit 0, silent, nothing changed
results.3: exit 3, `troupe: error: agents.reviewer: its whole value comes from include 'file:agents/reviewer.yaml' in /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml; change the included file instead`
results.4: exit 3, `troupe: agents.reviewer: value comes from include /theatre/.troupe/agents/reviewer.yaml with overrides; refusing to replace it (change a path inside it instead); no file changed`

context.in_practice: On every route, setting a text-file include actually wrote the new text into prompt.txt. Even route 1's description says it always refuses, but neither of its arms did. The routes only differed on YAML-file includes. There, routes 3 and 4 refused even when the value was unchanged. On routes 1 and 2, one arm refused and the other quietly accepted the unchanged value, so neither route behaved the same across its arms. On every route, `config history` afterwards was the same: four import entries plus a single `set` of prompt from "Be terse.\n" to "Be verbose.\n" by human:owner. No-ops and refusals were not logged.
context.stakes: Whether `config set` on a key whose whole value comes from an include (a text file such as `prompt: file:prompt.txt`, or a YAML file such as `coder: file:agents/coder.yaml`) writes into the included file or refuses. It also decides whether re-sending the value the key already has is a quiet no-op or an exit-3 error, which matters to scripts that re-apply the same config.
context.tradeoff: Refusing even unchanged values (routes 3 and 4, and one arm each of routes 1 and 2) means a script that re-applies the same config gets exit 3. Accepting them silently (the other arm of routes 1 and 2) avoids that, but the two arms of one route then act differently, and the text include is overwritten in place either way.

plan_why: Shows, for a text include and for scalar-form and mapping-form YAML includes, whether replacing the whole included value is refused (exit 3) even when the value is identical, treated as a no-op, or written into the text file in place
routes: Exit 3 always, even when the new value is identical (including changes through an ancestor)
Exit 3 only when the value would change; an identical value is a no-op
Rule 4 applies only to the root of a YAML include; a text include is edited in place
